tools.name: list_layers
tools.title: List layers
tools.description: List the layers of the open QGIS project that FilterMate knows, as {"layers": [...]}. Each layer has layer_id, name, provider_type, feature_count (-1 when unknown), geometry_type, crs_authid, layer_kind (vector, raster or point_cloud), has_active_filter and active_filter_expression. Call this first: the other tools take layer names or ids from it.

tools.name: filter_status
tools.title: Filter status
tools.description: Snapshot of the filter session: status, active_filters ({layer name: subset string}), their count, last_applied_at / last_applied_layer / last_applied_source and last_error. Vector subset strings only. filter_state also covers raster and point cloud layers.

tools.name: filter_state
tools.title: Filter state
tools.description: Every layer FilterMate filters right now, of any kind, as {"layers": [...]}. Each row has layer_id, name, layer_kind, subset (the filter string, empty for a clipped raster) and derived (true when the layer reads a clipped copy of its source). Use it to check what a filter did, and to find out what a previous call did when a request timed out.

tools.name: list_favorites
tools.title: List favorites
tools.description: List the favorites (saved filters) of the FilterMate project, as {"favorites": [...]}. Each has favorite_id (what apply_favorite takes), name, description, layer_name and expression.

tools.name: describe_layer
tools.title: Describe a layer
tools.description: What a filter can test on a layer: its fields, bands or point attributes. Returns layer_id, name, layer_kind, provider_type, crs_authid, geometry_type, feature_count, subset (its current filter), and by kind: fields [{name, type, alias, filterable}] for a vector layer (filterable is false for virtual and joined fields, which a filter expression cannot test); bands [{band, name, classes}] and pixel_size for a raster, classes [{value, label}] only on a paletted band; attributes [name] for a point cloud.

layer.description: Layer id or name, of any kind

tools.name: field_values
tools.title: Values of a field
tools.description: Distinct values a field really takes, among the features the layer shows now (its filter applies). Use it to write a filter with the exact spelling of a value. Returns values, truncated (more values exist), and minimum and maximum for a numeric or date field. NULL is left out. Refused on web services (WFS...), which would have to be read whole.

search.description: Text fields: only values containing this text, ignoring case

tools.name: preview_filter
tools.title: Try a filter
tools.description: Try a filter expression on a private copy of the layer: nothing changes in the project. It is what apply_filter would do, and it replaces the layer's current filter in the same way. Returns valid, feature_count (features kept, -1 when unknown) and error (the reason when valid is false). Refused on web services and memory layers, and for anything but a plain condition (subqueries, most functions).

tools.name: map_context
tools.title: Map context
tools.description: What the user is looking at in QGIS. Returns project_crs, canvas_crs, extent_wkt (the visible extent, usable as is with geometry_filter and canvas_crs), scale, active_layer_id, active_layer_name and selections [{layer_id, name, selected_count}] (the layers with selected features, which cross_filter uses as its source). available is false when QGIS has no map canvas.

tools.name: apply_filter
tools.title: Apply a filter expression
tools.description: Set the filter (subset string) of one vector layer; it replaces the layer's previous filter. Returns success and active_filters ({layer name: subset string} after the call). For spatial filtering between layers use cross_filter or geometry_filter. Revert with clear_filters. Caution: some providers (GeoPackage, Shapefile through OGR) accept an invalid SQL expression without any error and the layer then shows no feature. Check list_layers afterwards (feature_count -1, or 0 when you expected matches) and use clear_filters to recover.

layer_name.description: Name of a VECTOR layer (not its id; the first vector layer of that name is used)

expression.description: Subset string: the provider's SQL WHERE clause, without the WHERE keyword. For a PostgreSQL, GeoPackage, Shapefile or Spatialite layer: "population" > 10000 AND "dep" = '31'. Quote field names with double quotes and text values with single quotes.

source.description: Free-text tag shown in the FilterMate log to tell where the filter came from

tools.name: undo_filter
tools.title: Undo the last vector filter
tools.description: Undo the last step of the dock's vector filter history (the dock's Undo button). Returns the step rolled back to (layer_name, expression, is_clear) and active_filters. Only steps recorded by the dock itself are undone: nothing done through these tools (apply_filter, cross_filter, geometry_filter, point_cloud_filter, clear_filters, apply_favorite) is, so use clear_filters to revert those. Fails with 'Nothing to undo' when the history is empty. Not idempotent: each call undoes one more step, so after an error or a timeout read filter_state before calling again.

tools.name: redo_filter
tools.title: Redo the last undone vector filter
tools.description: Redo the step undone last in the dock's vector filter history (the dock's Redo button). Same answer and same caution as undo_filter (not idempotent: read filter_state after an error or a timeout). Fails with 'Nothing to redo' when there is nothing to redo.

tools.name: cross_filter
tools.title: Cross filter
tools.description: Filter layers by their spatial relation to a selection made on a source layer, any kind to any kind. Source kinds: a vector layer (its selected features), a raster (pixels kept by raster_selection, e.g. elevation between 1200 and 1300) or a point cloud (points kept by point_cloud_criteria, e.g. class 6). Targets keep what satisfies the predicates: vector features, raster pixels or LiDAR points inside the source area (outside with Disjoint). Filters apply in place to the project layers and replace the previous filter of each target unless operator is given. Not recorded in the undo history: revert with clear_filters. Returns filtered (names of the layers filtered), failed ({layer: reason}), skipped ({layer: reason}) and warnings ({layer: reason}: filtered, but a web service read up to its budget, so features may be missing). A layer that is not found is reported in failed; a source that is not found is an error.

source_layer.description: Source layer, vector, raster or point cloud: layer id or name

target_layers.description: Layers to filter, of any kind: layer ids or names. The source itself is not filtered (except with filter_source).

predicates.description: Spatial predicates, each tested as `target <predicate> source`: Intersect (share any space), Contain (the target contains the source), Disjoint (share nothing; rasters and point clouds then keep the outside of the source), Equal (same geometry), Touch (borders meet, interiors do not), Overlap (partial overlap of same-dimension geometries), Are within (the target lies inside the source), Cross (lines crossing). A target is kept when ANY listed predicate holds.

buffer.description: Buffer applied to the source geometry before testing, in the source CRS units (metres for a projected CRS; for a geographic CRS the API treats them as metres). Negative shrinks. 0 = none.

coverage_min.description: Polygon targets only: minimum share (%) of the target that must lie inside the source

operator.description: How to combine with the previous filter of each target: AND (keep what both filters keep), OR (keep what either keeps), AND NOT (remove the new selection from the previous filter). Omit to replace the previous filter.

selected_only.description: Vector source: use the features currently selected in QGIS (all features when none is selected; a web service source such as WFS must be selected or already filtered, it is never read whole). You cannot change the QGIS selection with these tools: ask the user to select the features, or use geometry_filter with a WKT geometry.

anyOf.description: Pixels kept on a raster source (same rules as the EXPLORING raster panel of the dock).

mode.description: range: pixels between minimum and maximum; classes: pixels whose value is in `classes`; expression: raster calculator expression

minimum.description: range: lower bound, inclusive (in band units)

maximum.description: range: upper bound, inclusive (in band units)

derivative.description: range only: quantity the bounds apply to. With anything but `value` the band is read as a DTM (elevation model) and the bounds are in degrees / percent / etc.

raster_selection.description: REQUIRED when the source is a raster: which pixels are the source area

anyOf.description: Points kept on a point cloud (ASPRS classes, ranges, return number, expression).

classes.description: ASPRS classification codes kept (0-255), e.g. 2 ground, 3-5 vegetation, 6 building, 9 water

z_min.description: Minimum Z (elevation), in the layer CRS units

z_max.description: Maximum Z (elevation), in the layer CRS units

expression.description: Point cloud expression (e.g. Classification = 6 AND Z > 1000), ANDed with the other criteria

point_cloud_criteria.description: Point cloud source: which points make the source area (omit = the points it shows now)

filter_source.description: Raster source: also mask the source raster outside the selection

tools.name: geometry_filter
tools.title: Filter by a WKT geometry
tools.description: Filter layers of any kind by a WKT geometry (a drawn area, an extent, a commune outline). Same effect and answer as cross_filter, with a geometry given inline instead of a source layer: the way to filter by an area when no source feature can be selected in QGIS. Replaces the previous filter of each target unless operator is given. Not in the undo history: revert with clear_filters. Returns filtered, failed, skipped and warnings.

crs.description: CRS of the geometry, authority code such as EPSG:2154 or EPSG:4326 (the coordinate order is x/longitude first)

target_layers.description: Layers to filter, of any kind: layer ids or names

predicates.description: Spatial predicates, each tested as `target <predicate> source`: Intersect (share any space), Contain (the target contains the source), Disjoint (share nothing; rasters and point clouds then keep the outside of the source), Equal (same geometry), Touch (borders meet, interiors do not), Overlap (partial overlap of same-dimension geometries), Are within (the target lies inside the source), Cross (lines crossing). A target is kept when ANY listed predicate holds.

buffer.description: Buffer applied to the geometry, in the units of the CRS of the first target

coverage_min.description: Polygon targets only: minimum share (%) of the target inside the geometry

operator.description: How to combine with the previous filter of each target: AND (keep what both filters keep), OR (keep what either keeps), AND NOT (remove the new selection from the previous filter). Omit to replace the previous filter.

tools.name: point_cloud_filter
tools.title: Filter point clouds
tools.description: Keep only some points (by class, elevation, intensity, return number or expression) on point cloud layers. The same criteria apply to every listed layer, e.g. all the tiles of a LiDAR HD dataset. Sets the layer filter (e.g. 'Classification = 6 AND Z >= 1000'). It is one step of the dock's history of those point clouds (the dock's Undo on the layer reverts it) but undo_filter does not undo it: revert with clear_filters. Returns done (layers filtered), failed and skipped.

layers.description: Point cloud layers (LiDAR tiles...): layer ids or names

criteria.description: Points to keep; at least one criterion is required

classes.description: ASPRS classification codes kept (0-255), e.g. 2 ground, 3-5 vegetation, 6 building, 9 water

z_min.description: Minimum Z (elevation), in the layer CRS units

z_max.description: Maximum Z (elevation), in the layer CRS units

expression.description: Point cloud expression (e.g. Classification = 6 AND Z > 1000), ANDed with the other criteria

operator.description: How to combine with the previous filter of each target: AND (keep what both filters keep), OR (keep what either keeps), AND NOT (remove the new selection from the previous filter). Omit to replace the previous filter. AND NOT needs an existing filter on each layer.

tools.name: clear_filters
tools.title: Clear filters
tools.description: Put layers back on their original source with no filter (the dock's Unfilter). Removes subset strings and restores the original source of raster and point cloud layers that were clipped. This is the way to revert cross_filter, geometry_filter, point_cloud_filter and apply_favorite. Returns done, failed and skipped.

layers.description: Layers of any kind to unfilter: layer ids or names

tools.name: apply_favorite
tools.title: Apply a favorite
tools.description: Apply a saved favorite, as the dock's favorites menu does. Returns the step (layer_name, expression, is_clear) and active_filters. The favorite id must exist: use list_favorites first.

tools.name: export_layers
tools.title: Export filtered layers
tools.description: Write layers, as filtered now, to files on the QGIS machine, below the server's export root. Writes files: a file with the same name already in the sub-folder is overwritten. The files stay on the machine running QGIS; the answer gives their paths there. Returns done (layers written), outputs ({layer name: file path}), failed and skipped.

layers.description: Layers of any kind to export as they are filtered now, one file per layer: ids or names

subfolder.description: Sub-folder of the export root configured on the QGIS machine (a or a/b, letters, digits, _ . - only, no .. and never an absolute path)

crs.description: Output CRS such as EPSG:2154 (omit = each layer's CRS)
